title: latency-aware-surge-governor-and-utilization-telemetry
author: Lydia Chen
description: Motivation: We regularly observe short-lived surge traffic that degrades tail latency for dedicated tenants when warm pools and burst tokens are consumed faster than the autoscaler can react. This PR introduces a "latency-aware surge governor" that: (1) detects short surges using a fast-timescale utilization envelope, (2) enforces conservative burst fencing when predicted tail latency exceeds tenant SLO, and (3) adjusts warm-pool headroom in a workload-aware manner to reduce oscillation. This also adds new utilization telemetry to aid capacity planning and post-incident debugging. Changes include an algorithmic governor in the autoscaler, a lightweight online calibration flow for per-tenant headroom, and a telemetry exporter that records percentile-backed utilization and surge events. Implementation notes: - The governor uses an exponentially-weighted maximum-utilization window (configurable), combined with a latency threshold derived from tenant SLOs. - When a surge is detected, the governor can temporarily fence burst allocations (soft deny) and trigger conservative warm-pool pre-warming for the affected tenant group. - The headroom calibrator tracks per-tenant effective concurrency distributions and proposes a shrunken or expanded warm pool size; proposals are logged and optionally autopromoted after a safety window. - Telemetry: new metrics are exposed (dedicated.surge_events, dedicated.surge_headroom_suggestion, dedicated.util_p50/p90/p99_by_tenant) and a compact event log is emitted to the central observability pipeline. Backwards compatibility: All new behaviors are behind feature flags and sensible defaults; operators can opt into the governor gradually. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached and discussed with SRE (ENG-2017) - [x] Unit tests for governor logic and calibrator - [x] E2E smoke test that simulates short surges and validates latency/backoff - [x] Metrics and labels added to telemetry pipeline - [x] Docs: short ops-readme and recommended tuning guide Commit summary: "add latency-aware surge governor, headroom calibrator, telemetry exporter" (squashed from 7 commits). Related work: builds on previous burst-token and warm-pool initiatives (see ENG-10234, ENG-14721) and complements the proactive scaler features. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to a small set of tenants on Dedicated, observability enabled, monitor p99 latency and surge_events. If regression appears, toggle the governor off and revert headroom proposals.
commits: 7 commits: 1) init surge governor core algorithm, 2) headroom calibrator skeleton + interfaces, 3) telemetry exporter and metric registration, 4) unit tests for EWMA envelope and surge detection, 5) e2e smoke harness and test data, 6) docs and feature flag config, 7) small followups and test fixes

review_comments: Aisha: 'Can you walk through the decision to soft-fence bursts instead of immediate hard deny? I'm worried about customer-visible throttles.' -- Lydia: 'Soft-fence allows a short backoff window; we log decisions and fall back to hard deny only when configured in strict mode. Added clarifying comments and a new config knob.'; Jon: 'Telemetry cardinality — per-tenant p99 might blow up metrics. Consider aggregation buckets.' -- Lydia: 'Telemetry uses a configurable aggregation window and bucketized tenant groups by quota tier to limit cardinality; updated exporter to group small tenants.'; Marta: 'Are proposals from the calibrator auto-applied? What safety checks exist?' -- Lydia: 'By default proposals are advisory; we added an opt-in auto_promote flag guarded by a 24h safety window and anomaly checks.'; Aisha (on tests): 'Need coverage for concurrent calibrator updates.' -- Lydia: 'Added a concurrency unit test and fixed a race.'
merge_result: merged by squash on 2024-11-20. Merge notes: squash and merge after CI green; no conflicts. Post-merge steps: enabled feature flag for internal staging cluster and added dashboard tiles for dedicated.surge_events and headroom_suggestions.
release_notes: Added latency-aware surge governor to autoscaler (feature-flagged). New telemetry metrics for surge events and headroom suggestions. Operators should validate p99 latency when enabling. See docs/ops/surge-governor-README.md for tuning guidance.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report unexpected TPS drops after enabling, first check dedicated.surge_events; if frequent soft-fences appear, toggle feature flag 'surge_governor.enabled' to false and review headroom_suggestion logs. Use /api/v1/admin/calibrator/proposals to inspect pending promotions.
internal_testing: Smoke tests simulate 10s-60s surges at 2x baseline; expected outcome: p99 latency rise < 2x and warm-pool pre-warm triggers within 5s of detection. All smoke tests passed in CI. Load-run on staging showed a 22% reduction in p99 spikes for test workloads.
additional_context: This PR is intentionally conservative: the governor prioritizes tenant tail latency over short-term throughput to improve customer experience during transient bursts. The telemetry additions were designed to be low-cardinality by default and to be opt-in at high granularity.
test_plan: Run unit tests; deploy to staging with feature flag on for three tenants; run surge_simulator for 24h; verify no unexpected evictions and that proposals are logged but not auto-applied unless enabled.
deployment_instructions: 1) Merge to main. 2) Turn on feature flag 'surge_governor.enabled' in staging via config map. 3) Monitor dedicated.surge_events and p99 latency dashboards. 4) Gradually include more tenants and consider enabling auto_promote after 48h of stable metrics.
pm_notes: PMs: This reduces customer-facing latency spikes during bursts; expected to reduce noise in support channel for dedicated tenants. Recommend communicating as an ops-level improvement rather than a customer-visible feature for the first rollout.
